subject.title: Feature: trustedWebhooks for Discord — allow specific webhooks to trigger agent responses

question: Should Discord accept a guild-scoped trusted webhook allowlist, and should that surface be allowed to map webhook payloads onto a Discord user identity?
rationale: The request is narrower than `allowBots: true`, but it makes webhook possession a new authority to enter agent sessions and the proposed user mapping crosses authorization and session-identity boundaries.

options.title: Approve allowlist only
options.body: Add a default-off webhook ID allowlist that can pass the bot-message gate, while deferring or rejecting webhook-to-user mapping until its authorization semantics are defined.

options.title: Approve constrained user mapping
options.body: Allow `mapToUser` only with strict validation against configured guild users, clear audit behavior, and tests proving it cannot bypass sender authorization or session isolation.

options.title: Decline Discord webhook ingress
options.body: Keep Discord bot-message policy unchanged and direct external automations to an authenticated webhook plugin or other explicitly owned integration path.

recommendation.title: Approve allowlist only
recommendation.body: Add a default-off webhook ID allowlist that can pass the bot-message gate, while deferring or rejecting webhook-to-user mapping until its authorization semantics are defined.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Discord preflight ownership and issue-timeline involvement make this the best available security/product routing candidate.
